prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot on request; consulted on electrical events), Main Transformer, export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere). Public grid, port ops out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; blocks protection-conflicting commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode if aux lost), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor; Turbine Sensor Bus collects measurements; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; produces Leading Edge Tile Image in close-range survey; shall repeat pass if coverage insufficient). Substation: Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling, not exported, sheds nonessential, start-failure alarm, UPS. Grid Dispatcher sets dispatch; Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard) allocates output, uses Position Quality Flag, assigns vessel/crew after Duty Planner confirms. Frequency response only in authorized mode; comms loss keeps local protection; alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; work packages from Pitch Deviation Notice; Session Revocation Receipt; forwards time-stamped observations to Shore Control Room (Amber Quay): escalates alerts, retains decision record/observations/outcome), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale), Operations Radio Console, Work Permit Portal (Redoubt?: shall block permit release until risk reviews and isolation refs complete), Personnel Tracking Console (crew accounted). Control Engineer validates data (stale = unverified, not sole basis for intrusive task), cross-checks, reassesses alert after field findings; findings compared with observations before closing. Blade Specialist reviews evidence. Duty Planner ranks, checks parts/limits, submits scope/location/crew/window. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy; Weather Analyst uses Wave Burst Record. Modes: Weather Hold (forecast alone doesn't release), Vessel Standby; withdraw personnel near limits. Vessel Master gets Transfer Manifest Addendum; Quiet Harbor blocks unauthorized route change. Crew Transfer Vessel uses Harness Audit Card (from HSE Officer) before transfer. Port Agent issues Berth Slot Confirmation. Storekeeper validates Backorder Exception Slip from Warehouse System (Mosslight). Permits: authorization not proof of safe state; HSE Officer confirms controls; Field Supervisor confirms method, active permit, independent isolation verification, briefs crew; Electrical Technician identifies isolations,

New part:
S333: A change in equipment condition, task scope, or operating constraint requires the Field Supervisor to pause work and reassess the authorization.
S334: The Duty Planner coordinates any revised work window with the relevant operational roles before the permit is amended.
S335: The Field Supervisor confirms that tools, temporary connections, and personnel are clear before requesting isolation removal.
S336: The Electrical Technician checks that the work area is ready for restoration and reports any outstanding defects or restrictions.
S337: The Substation Operator removes isolations only under the approved switching process and records each restoration action.
S338: The Control Engineer reviews the restored equipment state and confirms that required operational checks are complete.
S339: The Shore Control Room retains the permit status, isolation history, test results, and restoration decision for operational review.
S340: The Duty Planner closes the work authorization after the Field Supervisor confirms completion or formally records any remaining work.
S341: Equipment returns to service only when operating personnel accept the restored condition and any applicable restrictions are communicated.
S342: The Substation Operator maintains the Offshore Substation within approved operating limits and follows current switching instructions.
S343: At the start of each shift, the operator reviews alarms, active restrictions, equipment status, and handover notes.
S344: Routine rounds cover room temperature, ventilation, water ingress, lighting, access control, and visible signs of damage.
S345: The operator checks Main Transformer temperatures, cooling equipment, oil indications, and abnormal noise against established limits.
S346: The Export Cable Monitor is reviewed for trends or alarms that require escalation to the Control Engineer.
S347: The Grid Interface Relay is checked for healthy indications and consistency with the approved grid operating state.
S348: The SCADA Gateway displays are compared with local indications when equipment status is uncertain.
S349: The Control Engineer investigates unexplained discrepancies before operating personnel rely on remote indications.
S350: The Work Permit Portal is checked to confirm that active work authorizations and isolation boundaries remain current.
S351: The operator verifies that personnel access records are consistent with the planned work and current site occupancy.
S352: The Fire Detection Panel is checked for healthy status, active faults, and unobstructed access to response equipment.
S353: The Emergency Generator produces the Start Test Trace during its scheduled functional test.
S354: The operator confirms fuel level, starting battery condition, ventilation, and readiness of the Emergency Generator for loss of normal supply.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
